XXIII.}}</noinclude>out, and threvv off their garments, and cast dust into the aire, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=24}}† the Tribune commaunded him to be caried into the castel, and to be beaten with vvhippes, and that he should be tormented: to know for vvhat cause they did so crie at him. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=25}}† And vvhen they had bound him very straight vvith thongs, Paul saith to the Centurion standing by him: Is it lavvful for you to whippe a man that is a Romane and vncondemned? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=26}}† Vvhich the Centurion hearing, vvent to the Tribune, and told him, saying, Vvhat wilt thou doe? for this man is a citizen of Rome. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=27}}† And the Tribune comming, said to him, Tel me, art thou a Romane? But he said, Yea. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=28}}† And the Tribune answered, I obtained this citie vvith a great summe. And Paul said, But I was also borne to it.

{{verse|chapter=22|verse=29}}† Immediatly therfore they departed from him that vvere to torment him. The Tribune also feared after he vnderstoode that he was a citizē of Rome, and because he had bound him. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=30}}† But the next day meaning to know more diligently for vvhat cause he vvas accused of the Ievves, he loosed him, and commaunded the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ἀρχιερεῖς.}}∷ Priests to come together and al the Councel: & bringing forth Paul, he set him among them.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''As the people in the tumult, so also the very cheefe of the Ievves in their Councel shew them selues obstinate, and wilful persecutors of the truth in S. Pauls person. Whose behauiour towardes them is ful of constancie, modestie, and wisedom. 11 (Christ also by a vision encouraging him, and foretelling that he shal to Rome.) 12 Yea they conspire vvith 40 men to kil him traiterously. 16 But the matter being detected, the Romane Tribune conuaigheth him strongly to Cæsaréa.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=23|verse=1}}}}ND Paul looking vpon the Councel, said, Men brethren, I vvith al good conscience haue conuersed before God, vntil this present day. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=2}}† And the high Priest Ananias commaunded them that stoode by him, to smite him on the mouth. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=3}}† Then Paul said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He said not this through perturbation of minde or of a passion, but by way of prophecie, that this figuratiue high priesthod then trimmed like a whited wall, was to be destroied, where as now the true priesthod of Christ was ''cōe''.}}∷ God shal strike thee, thou whited vvall. And thou sitting iudgest me according to the lavv, and contrarie to lavv doest thou commaund me to be smitten? {{verse|chapter=23|verse=4}}† And they that stoode by, said, Doest thou reuile the high Priest of God? {{verse|chapter=23|verse=5}}† And Paul said, {{sup|‖}} I knewe not, brethren, that he is the high Priest. For it is written: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 22, 28.''}}* ''The prince of thy people thou shalt not misspeake''. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=6}}† And Paul<noinclude>{{rh|||knovving}}</noinclude>
